Draw the temporal and contemporaneous networks of a continuous time model

Source: R/ctGraph.R
ctNetworkPlot.Rd

Plots the networks ctNetwork computes, in the usual style of network psychometrics: signed edges with width by magnitude, arrowheads and self-loops on the directed temporal network, and no arrowheads on the undirected contemporaneous network.

Given more than one dt, the networks are drawn side by side at each interval, showing how the network a study finds depends on how often it measures.

Usage

ctNetworkPlot(
  x,
  dt = 1,
  state = NULL,
  networks = c("temporal", "contemporaneous"),
  threshold = 0,
  engine = c("ggplot", "qgraph"),
  maxwidth = 3,
  arrowsize = 2.6,
  nodesize = 10,
  labelsize = 3.2,
  poscolour = "#2166AC",
  negcolour = "#B2182B",
  title = "auto",
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A ctStanModel, a fit, or a ctNetwork from ctNetwork.

dt

One or more time intervals. Ignored, with a message, when x is already a ctNetwork.

state

Where state dependent cells are evaluated; see ctNetwork. Ignored, with a message, when x is already a ctNetwork. For a state dependent system the point appears in the plot's subtitle. A linear system gets no subtitle.

networks

Which networks to draw; see ctNetwork. Each network and each dt gets its own panel.

threshold

Edges with abs(weight) at or below this are not drawn.

engine

'ggplot' (the default) or 'qgraph'.

maxwidth

Line width of the largest edge drawn.

arrowsize

Arrowhead length in mm.

nodesize, labelsize

Node and label size.

poscolour, negcolour

Colours for positive and negative edges. The defaults are a colour-blind safe blue and red. For the common green and red, use 'darkgreen' and 'red'.

title

Panel title, or NULL for none. 'auto' names the source and the interval.

...

Passed to ctNetwork, or to qgraph::qgraph() when engine='qgraph'.

Value

A ggplot2 object, which can be modified further or printed. With engine='qgraph', the qgraph object, invisibly, after drawing it.

Details

Drawn with ggplot2. engine='qgraph' passes the weight matrix to qgraph::qgraph() instead, if that package is installed. The matrices from ctNetwork can also be passed to qgraph directly, as in qgraph::qgraph(ctNetwork(fit)$temporal, directed=TRUE).

Examples

m <- ctModel(type='ct', n.latent=3, n.manifest=3,
  manifestNames=c('y1','y2','y3'), latentNames=c('a','b','c'),
  LAMBDA=diag(3),
  DRIFT=matrix(c(-.4,0,0, .3,-.5,0, 0,.4,-.6), 3, 3, byrow=TRUE),
  DIFFUSION=matrix(c(1,0,0, .3,1,0, 0,-.4,1), 3, 3, byrow=TRUE))

# The indirect path a -> b -> c is invisible at a short interval and present
# at a long one -- the same model, two networks.
ctNetworkPlot(m, dt=c(.2, 2), networks='temporal')
